claims.context_count: Whiskering an Exchange path with arbitrary fixed prefix/suffix preserves its expanded swap count, including the list-associativity casts.
claims.old_invariant: Every cell generated by the old involution/braid/far forms and all old pasting/context closures preserves swap-count parity.
claims.verified_incompleteness: The actual language permits repeated operation IDs. With one read-only Unit operation and word [(),()], one checked self-swap is a loop with count 1; reflexivity has count 0. No old ExchangeHigher cell connects them. Thus the three-form relation does not connect every pair of parallel Exchange paths.
claims.condition: A self-exchange accepted by the read/write checker forces the operation write set to be empty.
claims.operational_law: Any total PMF action with that empty write set preserves the complete store. This is uniform in every permitted kernel; no assumption of deterministic private sampling is made.
claims.extension: ExchangeHigherWithSelf embeds all old higher cells and adds one bounded self-exchange contraction (one swap versus zero), with reversal, pasting and surrounding-context closures.
claims.counterexample_closed: The former missing contraction is constructed as explicit data in the extension; it remains formally non-derivable in the old three-form relation.

scope: Incompleteness is relative to the goal that ALL parallel paths of this repeated-ID word syntax should be connected. It is not a refutation of standard braid/symmetric relations in a different occurrence-aware presentation.
The added higher root expresses a chosen additional identification in the current store semantics. It does not identify arbitrary supplied paths.
Only this parity obstruction is removed; no global coherence/completeness or finite derivation type result is established for the extension.
Structural path laws, all critical overlaps, full heterogeneous cryptographic boxes, copy/discard coherence and approximate-game transformations remain outstanding.
No new actual MAC execution change or nontrivial MAC query reordering is claimed. Earlier full MAC/caller laws remain unchanged.
Store semantics is total and discrete; private erased random draws and CPU timing are not observations unless explicitly encoded as writes. No native runtime guarantee is transferred.
One-versus-zero swap counts are primitive proof-rule counts, not kernel bytes, shared-DAG size, runtime or an exclusive higher-dimensional advantage.
novelty: Unconfirmed. A concrete incompleteness theorem and explicit extension of this implementation are verified; publication priority and the full research goal remain unresolved.
